content.user_title: Build Azure Cosmos DB Apps with TypeScript
content.value_statement: Azure Cosmos DB development requires correct authentication, partition keys, queries, and failure handling. This skill provides practical TypeScript patterns for common data plane operations.
actual_capabilities: Explains Azure AD, account key, and connection string authentication patterns.
Shows create, read, replace, upsert, delete, and patch operations for documents.
Builds parameterized, paginated, and cross-partition Cosmos DB queries.
Demonstrates bulk operations across create, read, replace, upsert, patch, and delete actions.
Covers simple and hierarchical partition key definitions.
Provides patterns for errors, ETags, optimistic concurrency, and a typed service layer.
limitations: Covers the Cosmos DB NoSQL data plane, not Azure Resource Manager account provisioning.
Provides reference patterns but does not connect to or inspect a live Azure account.
Requires project-specific validation for partition strategy, throughput, indexing, and cost.
Examples target Node.js 20 or later and @azure/cosmos version 4.9.0.

use_cases.title: Create a Cosmos DB service
use_cases.description: Design a typed service layer for document creation, lookup, updates, deletion, and category queries.

use_cases.title: Review data access patterns
use_cases.description: Check authentication, parameterized queries, partition keys, retries, and ETag handling before deployment.

use_cases.title: Plan high-volume writes
use_cases.description: Select bulk operation patterns and partition keys for workloads with many document changes.

prompt_templates.title: Connect with Azure AD
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to connect a Node.js TypeScript application to Cosmos DB with DefaultAzureCredential and named environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Build typed document operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a typed Cosmos DB service for [entity] with create, read, patch, replace, upsert, and delete methods.

prompt_templates.title: Design a safe query
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a parameterized query for [filter requirements]. Include pagination, partition key usage, and handling for rate limits.

prompt_templates.title: Review a production data layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Cosmos DB access design for authentication, partitioning, bulk writes, ETags, retries, disposal, scalability, and cost risks.

output_examples.input: Plan secure authentication for a TypeScript API running in Azure.
output_examples.output: A setup plan using DefaultAzureCredential, a named endpoint variable, required Azure roles, startup validation, and account key avoidance.

output_examples.input: Design product lookup by category and maximum price.
output_examples.output: A parameterized query approach scoped by category, with pagination guidance and notes about request units and cross-partition costs.
A workflow that reads the item ETag, applies conditional replacement, handles precondition failures, and preserves conflicting updates.

best_practices: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential and assign only the required Cosmos DB data roles.
Use parameterized queries and include partition keys whenever the access pattern permits.
Handle rate limits, ETag conflicts, missing documents, and client disposal explicitly.
anti_patterns: Do not embed account keys, connection strings, or production endpoints in source code.
Do not use broad cross-partition queries without reviewing request unit cost.
Do not replace shared documents without ETag checks when concurrent updates are possible.

faq.question: Does this skill provision Azure Cosmos DB accounts?
faq.answer: No. It covers data plane operations with @azure/cosmos, not management plane provisioning with @azure/arm-cosmosdb.

faq.question: Which authentication method is recommended?
faq.answer: Use DefaultAzureCredential with Azure role assignments when possible. Account keys and connection strings need stronger secret controls.

faq.question: Does it support hierarchical partition keys?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows a MultiHash partition key with multiple paths and the corresponding item lookup format.

faq.question: Can it help prevent query injection?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use named query parameters instead of joining untrusted values into query text.

faq.question: Does it cover bulk writes?
faq.answer: Yes. It demonstrates mixed bulk operations and checking each operation result.

faq.question: Will the examples work without modification?
faq.answer: No. Replace sample identifiers, define project types, configure credentials, and test partitioning, indexing, throughput, and failure behavior.
